localization.name: ADI-2 Companion
localization.subtitle: Parametric EQ and MIDI control
localization.promotional_text: Build five-band EQ profiles, keep a local profile library and follow ADI-2 DAC volume changes. Native Mac controls, offline editing and demo mode included.
localization.description:
Build a five-band EQ profile on your Mac, keep your settings organized, and control your RME ADI-2 DAC through USB MIDI.

ADI-2 Companion is an independent native Mac app for listening setups that use an ADI-2 DAC. Shape each band with frequency, gain, Q and filter-type controls, and inspect the combined response curve before applying a profile to your output.

PROFILE EDITING
• Edit five parametric bands with a response graph and precise numeric controls.
• Import Equalizer APO or REW filter text, CSV filter data, and compatible JSON profiles.
• Review warnings when an import needs fewer bands or adjusted values.
• Keep profiles in a local library and export JSON copies to share or back up.
• Build and edit profiles offline without connecting hardware.

HARDWARE CONTROL
• Connect explicitly through USB MIDI and read the device settings before controls become available.
• Adjust output volume in 0.1 dB steps with keyboard and accessibility controls.
• Follow front-panel volume changes with a smoothly moving fader.
• Review EQ changes as a draft before choosing Apply to both output channels.

Explore the app in its clearly marked demo mode when your DAC is not connected. Demo mode sends no MIDI.

REQUIREMENTS AND CURRENT LIMITS
macOS 14 or later. Hardware control requires an RME ADI-2 DAC with compatible MIDI-control firmware, a USB connection, and MIDI Control enabled on the device. The app does not record or process playback audio, change the Mac's sample rate, or turn the DAC on remotely.

Device EQ-slot and setup-memory controls are marked Experimental in this build and have not yet been verified with connected hardware. ADI-2 Pro and ADI-2/4 Pro hardware have not yet been qualified with this Mac build.

No accounts, advertising or telemetry. Profiles stay on your Mac unless you export or share them yourself.

Independent software. Not affiliated with or endorsed by RME. Product names identify compatible hardware and belong to their respective owners.
localization.review_notes:
ADI-2 Companion is an independent local macOS EQ editor and USB MIDI controller. It is intended for ADI-2 DAC owners and people preparing five-band EQ profiles offline. It is a paid upfront, one-time purchase with no in-app purchases or subscriptions. It is not RME's official Remote application. The icon and interface artwork are original.

No account or reviewer login is needed. There is no subscription flow, network backend, audio capture, privileged helper or driver installer. The app uses the macOS App Sandbox and user-selected file read/write access. Its local profile library is stored inside its sandbox container.

WITHOUT HARDWARE
Choose Explore demo in the sidebar, or Device > Explore Demo in the menu bar. Keep the visible demo banner in view. Select an output and edit the EQ bands; Apply in demo updates simulated state only. Import/Export and local profile Save/Load work with local files. Loading a local profile creates a draft and does not send MIDI.

WITH HARDWARE
Use a physical ADI-2 DAC connected to the Mac by USB. Enable MIDI Control on the device; current DAC documentation places it under Remap Keys/Diag, with wording dependent on firmware. Select the DAC's MIDI endpoint and click Connect. The app reads fresh output/EQ state before enabling writes. Sync reads hardware settings again. Output volume and enabled parameter controls write immediately. EQ edits remain drafts until Apply EQ to both channels is chosen.

DEVICE MEMORY
The separate Profiles and device memory view contains 20 EQ slots and 9 device setups. These operations are visibly marked Experimental and are not yet hardware-qualified. Every live recall/save requires confirmation. An EQ-slot recall changes live EQ and replaces the editor draft; setup recall can change device-wide volume and routing. EQ-slot saves contain five bands, not Bass/Treble or Loudness switches. Setup saves use current hardware state, excluding unapplied drafts.

VALIDATION RECORDED SO FAR
Physical ADI-2 DAC on Apple silicon with macOS 27.2: MIDI discovery, a complete 219-parameter read, and a 0.1 dB Phones-volume reduction/restoration with fresh readback passed. The user also confirmed smooth live feedback while turning the DAC's physical volume knob. These observations do not establish Pro/2/4 compatibility, persistent-memory reliability, EQ Apply readback, or all supported Mac/OS combinations.

A physical-camera hardware interaction video, the exact tested final-build/device/firmware list, and the review contact must accompany the submission. Demo mode does not replace the required hardware video.
